title: Client-side span batcher with best-effort durable fallback and sketch-based telemetry
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: mobile and edge clients produce bursty spans that create load spikes and transient failures at the OTLP ingress. Existing server-side batching and back-pressure mitigations reduce load after the fact, but do not prevent initial overload and unnecessarily increase p99 latencies for customer requests.

Goal: ship a thin, cross-platform client-side span batcher (Go/Node/Python SDK wrappers) that: 1) batches and compresses spans client-side according to workload; 2) provides a small, best-effort on-disk durable fallback queue for transient network outages (configurable size and TTL); 3) emits lightweight sketch-based telemetry (approximate per-tenant span cardinality, dropped/span-size distributions) to help the collector apply informed sampling and routing; 4) integrates with our OTLP gateway using a negotiated header for payload hints (compression, sketch-previews).

Constraints and non-goals: we are not replacing server-side durability or long-term replay; on-disk fallback is bounded and best-effort only. Client library must not require changes to existing application instrumentation and must default to conservative resource usage on mobile/low-memory devices.

Why now: load spikes from a new mobile SDK release caused tempo ingest throttles and a brief degradation for premium tenants. Early batching at the client should reduce ingestion bursts and improve end-to-end p99 latency while giving better signals to routing and sampling components.
acceptance_criteria: Client-side library (Go + Node) that automatically batches spans and sends OTLP grpc/http with configurable window/size settings
On-disk fallback queue that preserves up to configured bytes or span count and is used only when network writes fail; queue evicts oldest entries beyond TTL
Sketch telemetry export: approximate cardinality and heavy-hitter estimates emitted every minute to collector with <5% overhead
End-to-end test demonstrating a 30% reduction in ingest burst RPS during synthetic mobile spike compared to no-client-batching
Integration tests and a canary rollout plan for mobile SDKs + OTLP gateway; instrumentation for monitoring queue utilization and client-induced errors
Documentation (README + Quickstart + config knobs) and migration guide for customers to opt into client batching
tasks: Design doc: batching semantics, eviction policy, and sketch format (Confluence)
Implement Go client wrapper: batching, compression (zstd), on-disk queue abstraction
Implement Node client wrapper: mirror semantics with platform IO limits
Add sketch exporter (HyperLogLog + Count-Min sketch) and collector ingestion hook to decode previews
Extend OTLP gateway to accept payload-hint headers and expose routing metrics
E2E performance harness: synthetic mobile spike scenario + canary dashboard
Create feature flag and rollout plan for 2% -> 10% -> 50% of mobile clients
